---
title: "Env.AlreadyRan"
description: "Atomic check-and-set gate for one-time-per-key execution."
---

Atomic check-and-set. Returns `1` if `key` was already set to a non-zero `int`; otherwise writes `Int=1` for the key and returns `0`. Intended as a "run once" gate across execute commands.

## Signature

```enforce
static proto native int AlreadyRan(string key);
```

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| key | `string` | The key to gate on. |

## Returns

`1` if a non-zero `Int` was already stored at `key`; `0` on the first call (after which the key now holds `Int=1`).

## Behavior

Atomic against other writers — the operation is performed under the store lock and is not subject to read-modify-write races between executes. The native only treats an `Int`-typed non-zero value as "already ran". A prior [Env.SetString](./setstring) for the same key is ignored — `AlreadyRan` will still take the first-call path and store `Int=1`, replacing the kind.

## Edge cases

- A prior [Env.SetString](./setstring) on the same key does not count as "already ran" — the call still writes `Int=1`, replacing the kind.
- A prior [Env.SetBool](./setbool) / [Env.SetFloatBits](./setfloatbits) on the same key does not count either.
- Returns `0` on the first call; the key is then set to `Int=1`. The gate is satisfied for every subsequent call regardless of intervening [Env.Erase](./erase) (which would clear the gate).
- Writing past the 256-entry cap on the first call is a silent no-op, so the gate would not actually be set. The next call would also report `0`. There is no diagnostic.

## Example

```enforce
class Demo {
    void Run() {
        if (Env.AlreadyRan("init")) {
            Console.Log("already ran, skipping the slow thing");
            return;
        }
        // …do the slow thing…
    }
}
```
